key_insight: In this hypersonic shock/turbulent boundary-layer interaction, finite-rate chemistry matters more than caloric effects: reacting flow predicts a smaller bubble, cooler post-shock field, and weaker reflected shock than simplified gas models.
engineering_relevance: For hypersonic vehicle design, using a frozen/chemically reacting model can materially change predicted heat loads and separation behavior, while thermally vs calorically perfect assumptions are secondary in this regime.
method: Three DNS cases with identical geometry and freestream conditions.
Compared a finite-rate reactive model against thermally perfect and calorically perfect single-species models.
Assessed separation, wall heat flux, shock angle, temperature fields, and turbulence-chemistry coupling.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic model differences in bubble size, wall heat flux, mean/fluctuating temperatures, and shock inclination, with turbulent Damköhler numbers reaching order unity in the recirculation region.
watch_item: The conclusions are specific to one high-enthalpy, Mach 6.4 configuration, so model hierarchy may shift outside this flow regime or geometry.
paper_title: Effects of thermochemical modelling on a hypersonic shock-wave/turbulent boundary-layer interaction
